TS | founded = {{Start date and age|df=yes|1967|8|2}} | dissolved = | stadium = [[Şenol Güneş Sports Complex|Papara Park]] | capacity = 40,980 | coordinates = {{Coord|40.999167|39.645833|format=dms|type:landmark_scale:3000_region:TR|display=it}} | chrtitle = President | chairman = Ertuğrul Doğan | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Thomas Reis ]] | league = {{Turkish football updater|Trabzonspor}} | season = {{Turkish football updater|Trabzonspor2}} | position = {{Turkish football updater|Trabzonspor3}} | current = 2026–27 Trabzonspor season | website = {{URL|https://www.trabzonspor.org.tr/|trabzonspor.org.tr}} | pattern_la1 = _trabzonspor2627h | pattern_b1 = _trabzonspor2627h | pattern_ra1 = _trabzonspor2627h | pattern_sh1 = _trabzonspor2627h | pattern_so1 = | leftarm1 = 5a1129 | body1 = 5a1129 | rightarm1 = 5a1129 | shorts1 = 5a1129 | socks1 = 5a1129 | pattern_la2 = _trabzonspor2627a | pattern_b2 = _trabzonspor2627a | pattern_ra2 = _trabzonspor2627a | pattern_sh2 = _trabzonspor2627a | pattern_so2 = | leftarm2 = 74b7e6 | body2 = 74b7e6 | rightarm2 = 74b7e6 | shorts2 = 74b7e6 | socks2 = 74b7e6 | pattern_la3 = _trabzonspor2627t | pattern_b3 = _trabzonspor2627t | pattern_ra3 = _trabzonspor2627t | pattern_sh3 = _trabzonspor2627t | pattern_so3 = | leftarm3 = 000000 | body3 = 000000 | rightarm3 = 000000 | shorts3 = 000000 | socks3 = 000000 }} {{Trabzonspor sections}} '''Trabzonspor Kulübü''' is a Turkish professional [[sports club]] located in the city of [[Trabzon]], located in [[Black Sea region|northeastern]] [[Turkey]]. Established in 1967 through the merger of several local clubs, Trabzonspor is one of the most prominent [[Association football|football clubs]] in [[Football in Turkey|Turkish history]]. The men’s football team has won seven [[Süper Lig]] championships, making Trabzonspor the first non-[[Istanbul]]-based club to achieve this feat in the [[Turkish football league system|Turkish league system]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablest/turkchamp.html|title=Turkey – List of Champions|date=28 May 2015|publisher=[[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|RSSSF]]|access-date=29 August 2015|archive-date=7 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230207082756/https://www.rsssf.org/tablest/turkchamp.html|url-status=live}} In addition to their football achievements, Trabzonspor also operates a [[Trabzonspor (women's football)|women’s football team]], a [[Trabzonspor B.K.|men’s basketball team]], and several other sports branches, reinforcing its status as a multi-sport club. Trabzonspor rose to prominence in the 1970s and 1980s, dominating [[Football in Turkey|Turkish football]] with six league titles between the [[1975–76 1.Lig|1975–76]] and [[1983–84 1.Lig|1983–84 seasons]]. This golden era marked the club as a powerhouse, with Trabzonspor becoming a symbol of regional pride and the only club to challenge the dominance of [[Istanbul]]-based teams, such as [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)|Fenerbahçe]], [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]], and [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]].{{cite web|url=https://www.trabzonspor.org.tr/en/club/history|title=Club History|publisher=Trabzonspor|access-date=3 May 2019|archive-date=20 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200920200639/https://www.trabzonspor.org.tr/en/club/history|url-status=live}} During this period, they also won nine [[Turkish Cup|Turkish Cups]], including a streak of three consecutive league titles in [[1978–79 1.Lig|1978–79]], [[1979–80 1.Lig|1979–80]], and [[1980–81 1.Lig|1980–81]]. After their sixth league title in [[1983–84 1.Lig|1983–84]], Trabzonspor endured a 38-year championship drought, marked by near-misses and structural rebuilding. This drought ended triumphantly in the [[2021–22 Süper Lig|2021–22 season]], as Trabzonspor clinched their seventh league title, led by a strong squad and under the management of [[Abdullah Avcı]]. The victory sparked massive celebrations across the city and reaffirmed the club’s status as one of Turkey’s most decorated and respected teams. The club’s colors are claret and sky blue, reflected in their iconic striped shirts, symbolizing the identity and culture of the [[Trabzon Province|Trabzon region]]. Trabzonspor has played its home matches at the [[Şenol Güneş Sports Complex]] (known as Papara Park for sponsorship reasons) since the [[2016–17 Süper Lig|2016–17 season]], a state-of-the-art stadium that replaced the historic [[Hüseyin Avni Aker Stadium]].[http://www.tff.org/Default.aspx?pageId=28&kulupId=3596 TRABZONSPOR A.Ş.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151203011928/http://www.tff.org/Default.aspx?pageId=28&kulupID=3596 |date=2015-12-03 }} tff.org {{in lang|tr}}, accessed 23 May 2010"}}
